content.overview: Section 45 requires that every share in a company having a share capital be distinguished by its distinctive number, except where shares are held by a person in dematerialised form under the Depositories Act, 1996.
content.glance: Every share must have a distinctive number, except dematerialised shares under the Depositories Act.
content.study: Every share in a company having a share capital shall be distinguished by its distinctive number. Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in such share in the records of a depository. Current-law framing: physical/certificated shares require distinctive numbers; demat shares under the Depositories Act are excepted.

sections.heading: Distinctive Number Rule
sections.body: Every share in a company having a share capital must be distinguished by its distinctive number.

sections.heading: Demat Exception
sections.body: The requirement does not apply to shares held in dematerialised form where the holder’s name is entered as beneficial owner in the depository’s records.

examples.title: Certificated shares numbered
examples.body: A company issues physical share certificates with distinctive numbers for each share. Section 45 is complied with.

examples.title: Demat shares
examples.body: Shares held in a demat account under the Depositories Act need not carry distinctive numbers under s. 45.

hypotheticals.question: Must dematerialised shares be numbered?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso to s. 45 excludes shares held with a depository where the holder is entered as beneficial owner.

distinctions.title: Numbering of shares (s. 45) vs certificate of shares (s. 46)
distinctions.right: Certificate as prima facie evidence of title

misconceptions.trap: All shares, including demat, must have distinctive numbers under s. 45.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso excludes dematerialised shares held through a depository.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 45 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify form of holding (certificated or demat). II. Apply distinctive-number rule or proviso. III. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Holding form; numbering compliance or demat exception; precise relief.

examTips: State the rule and the demat proviso.
